newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD vows to block German coalition tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: SPD vows to block German coalition tax reforms.

text.p: Oskar Lafontaine, leader of Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD), said on Wednesday that he would not go along with government plans to pass big tax cuts in 1999.

Speaking after cross-party talks on tax reform talks failed, Lafontaine said: "We will not have a tax lie on the statute books in 1999." The SPD can block most tax measures through its majority in the upper house of parliament.
"It is a reform against the people and against the economy," he told reporters.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel said earlier that he would press ahead with his legislative agenda to pass 30 billion marks in tax cuts -- which would take place in 1998 and 1999 -- through the lower house of parliament by the summer break.
The SPD had linked its readiness to accept coalition tax cuts to an agreement to cut occupational insurance charges from this summer, but this was refused by the government.

SPD parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping said he would now initiate legislation to cut such contributions by a gross 30 billion marks in 1998. He said the net relief to contribution payers would be between seven and 10 billion marks.
